message.content:
The email arrived on a Tuesday, sandwiched between a reminder for his dentist appointment and a promotional offer for artisanal dog biscuits (courtesy of his mother, ever vigilant about Winston’s well-being). "Northwood High Reunion – Let's Make It Happen!" the subject line blared. Noel almost deleted it. High school reunions. A veritable minefield of awkward small talk, questionable fashion choices, and the persistent feeling that everyone else had their lives figured out. He hadn't even been *that* fond of Northwood.

He scrolled through the body of the message, a hastily written plea from the Northwood Alumni Association. Apparently, the last reunion had been… lackluster. Low attendance, a DJ who specialized in polka music (seriously?), and a general air of melancholy hung over the proceedings. They were desperate. Desperate enough to reach out to former students, even those, like Noel, who hadn’t exactly excelled at remembering birthdays, let alone coordinating large-scale events. 

The person spearheading the revival was a woman named Vivian Sterling, the current president of the Alumni Association. Noel vaguely remembered her – a year ahead of him, captain of the debate team, perpetually radiating an aura of quiet competence. Her email was all business: a request for volunteers to join the reunion planning committee, outlining various roles from decorations to catering to, most dauntingly, "logistics and outreach."

He stared at the screen, Winston nudging his hand, demanding attention. He'd been avoiding commitments lately, burying himself in his work as a freelance graphic designer. But something about the email, the sheer earnestness of it, resonated. Maybe it was the memory of his own somewhat lonely high school experience and the desire to prevent others from feeling the same. Or maybe it was just a desperate need to shake up his routine.

With a sigh, and a silent apology to his burgeoning to-do list, he clicked “Reply.” “Happy to help,” he typed, adding a hesitant, “Let me know what’s needed.” He braced himself for the inevitable flood of emails and phone calls. Little did he know, he was about to step into a world of forgotten rivalries, resurfaced crushes, and a surprisingly complex web of Northwood High history.

The first meeting was scheduled for next week at the local library. He pictured a room full of slightly paunchy former football stars and overly enthusiastic cheerleaders, reminiscing about glory days long past. He hoped Vivian Sterling would be there to keep things organized. He briefly wondered if anyone he actually *liked* from high school was even going to attend. 

He added the meeting to his calendar, a small knot of apprehension tightening in his stomach. He really should have thought this through. But as he clicked "save," he couldn't quite shake the feeling that this reunion, for better or worse, was about to become more than just a night of awkward reminiscing.
